{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "ULTRA FULL PROMPT — Create a warm premium static landing page in Nuxt 3 for an edtech review website called \"StudyNest Reviews\". It should feel like a Xiaohongshu / Little Red Book inspired discovery page but adapted for education: cozy, social, trustworthy, card-based, warm cream background, coral accents, soft shadows, rounded stickers, handwritten highlights, review snippets, cute badges, teacher/student vibe, not corporate SaaS cold. IMPORTANT: this is a pure static front-end website only. No backend, no auth, no database, no real APIs, no live data, no login, no accounts, no CRUD. Use mock/static/sample content directly in the page/components. All interactions must be client-side visual only and should work in a static render. Build as a Nuxt landing page that can be opened and viewed without external services. MAIN GOAL: landing page for a review-site where parents, students, tutors, and adult learners discover and compare online learning platforms, courses, apps, bootcamps, language schools, tutoring services, test prep programs, coding courses, and study tools. The page must look polished enough for a real startup pitch. STYLE: warm, editorial, modern, social commerce, Xiaohongshu feed reference, cute but not childish, cream + peach + berry + honey + matcha palette. Avoid generic blue SaaS look. Use gradients, textured paper cards, washi-tape labels, rounded photo placeholders, star ratings, quote bubbles, tags, ranking chips, and soft sticky-note UI. TECH: Nuxt 3 + Vue components, static content, responsive CSS. You can use local arrays for review data. If images are needed, use gradient placeholders or CSS blocks with initials/icons, do not require external image APIs. PAGE STRUCTURE: 1) Top navigation: logo \"StudyNest\", nav links Reviews, Rankings, Parent Picks, Study Guides, Compare, CTA button \"Explore Reviews\". Add a small pill saying \"2026 learner-loved picks\". Header should be sticky with translucent warm glass effect. 2) HERO SECTION: headline: \"Find learning platforms people actually love using.\" Subheadline: \"Real-feeling reviews, cozy rankings, and side-by-side notes for online courses, tutoring, language apps, coding bootcamps, test prep, and study tools.\" Primary CTA \"Browse top-rated picks\" Secondary CTA \"See review wall\". Add trust mini metrics: \"420+ mock reviews\", \"68 edtech brands\", \"12 learning categories\", \"No sponsored ranking mockup\". Right side hero: Xiaohongshu-style stacked review cards with star ratings, student avatars as colored circles, course category chips, mini screenshots, floating badges like \"Parent approved\", \"Best for ADHD-friendly study\", \"Top coding pick\", \"Warm UX score 9.4\". Make it visually rich. 3) REVIEW WALL / DISCOVERY FEED: Masonry-like grid of review cards inspired by Xiaohongshu. Cards should include title, category, rating, short story-like review, pros chips, cons chips, learner type, price signal ($, $$, $$$), and a save/heart visual button. Use static sample review content for at least 12 cards. Make categories mixed: Language Learning, Math Tutoring, Coding Bootcamp, Exam Prep, Kids Reading, Note-taking App, Homeschool Support, Design Course, AI Study Assistant (but no real AI API), University Prep, Music Lessons, Career Certificates. 4) DRAG-AND-DROP INTERACTION SECTION: MUST include a static front-end drag-and-drop comparison board. Title: \"Build your own shortlist\". Users should be able to drag mock course/platform cards between columns: \"Curious\", \"Shortlisted\", \"Maybe Later\". This is only visual/local state, no saving, no backend. Include 8 draggable cards with rating, category, learner fit, and small tags. Make drag handles obvious. Add helper text: \"Try dragging cards — this demo keeps everything in your browser only.\" If full drag library is not wanted, implement with native HTML5 drag events or lightweight Vue logic. It must feel smooth and polished. 5) FEATURED RANKINGS: Horizontal ranking panels: \"Best for busy parents\", \"Best for self-paced coding\", \"Best cozy language app\", \"Best exam prep structure\", \"Best budget-friendly option\". Each ranking card should have rank number, score breakdown bars for Clarity, Motivation, Community, Value, Warmth. Use static scores. 6) COMPARISON TABLE: Clean responsive comparison of 6 fictional edtech products. Columns: Platform, Best For, Avg Rating, Learning Style, Price Feel, Review Mood, Standout Feature. On mobile it should become stacked cards. 7) REVIEW QUALITY SECTION: Explain how reviews are organized, with 4 steps: \"Collect learner context\", \"Separate hype from helpful\", \"Score the learning fit\", \"Summarize in plain language\". Keep wording friendly and transparent. Mention that all content is sample/static for the prototype. 8) CATEGORY TABS OR FILTER CHIPS: Add visual filter chips at top of feed: All, Kids, Teens, Adults, Coding, Languages, Test Prep, Budget, Parent-loved, Self-paced. Clicking can just filter local static cards if easy, otherwise visual active state is enough, but better if functional with local arrays. No backend. 9) TESTIMONIAL STRIP: warm quotes from fictional users: parent, high school student, career switcher, tutor. Include small avatar initials and rating. 10) NEWSLETTER / CTA: Static form UI only, no submission backend. If user clicks submit, show a small front-end-only success toast or inline message like \"Thanks! Static demo only — no email was sent.\" CTA copy: \"Get the cozy review digest\". 11) FOOTER: columns for Explore, Categories, Resources, About. Add disclaimer: \"Static prototype with sample reviews only.\" VISUAL DIRECTION DETAILS: Background #FFF7ED or #FFF5E8, cards white/cream, accents coral #FF7A6B, berry #B84A62, honey #F6B84B, matcha #8BAA6A, ink #2B2523. Use soft gradients, paper grain feel via CSS radial gradients, rounded 24px cards, subtle shadows, sticker labels rotated -2deg/2deg, cute star icons, bookmark shapes, little doodle lines via CSS. Typography: elegant friendly headings, readable body. Use large hero type, clear hierarchy. Layout should be responsive desktop/tablet/mobile. COMPONENT IDEAS: AppHeader.vue, HeroSection.vue, ReviewFeed.vue, DraggableShortlist.vue, RankingsSection.vue, ComparisonTable.vue, MethodSection.vue, Testimonials.vue, NewsletterCta.vue, AppFooter.vue. If making one file is easier, still keep code clean. INTERACTION DETAILS: Drag-and-drop board should not require server persistence. Cards should visibly change while dragging. Columns should highlight on dragover. After drop, card moves to new column. Add reset button \"Reset shortlist\". Also add hearts/bookmarks on review cards toggled locally, and category chips can filter locally. All data should be hardcoded. CONTENT REQUIREMENTS: Use realistic but fictional names, not real companies. Example platform names: LumaLingua, CodeSprout Studio, MathMochi, ReadCloud Kids, ExamBloom, SkillPorch, TutorTide, NoteNest Academy, BrightBridge Prep, MelodyMinute, DesignPatch, CareerCove. Do NOT use real brand logos. Use simple CSS icons/emojis if needed. ACCESSIBILITY: semantic sections, buttons not divs where interactive, keyboard visible focus styles, sufficient contrast, alt text for decorative placeholder images can be empty or aria-hidden, responsive tap targets. PERFORMANCE: no huge dependencies, no external image loading necessary. FINAL DELIVERABLE: a complete Nuxt static landing page design with warm Xiaohongshu-inspired edtech review-site look, complex enough to feel real, with static mock data, local-only drag and drop shortlist, local-only filters/bookmarks/toast, and no backend/API/auth/database at all.",
 "judge": {
  "model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8",
  "model_sha": "94125d2bd83076b21eed33119525e29eaf3894f4",
  "request_model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8:novita",
  "provider": "novita",
  "pinned_on": "2026-10-09",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "rubric_id": "rva1:mean(visual,query,asset)"
 }
}

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
